title: KATO: Knowledge Alignment And Transfer for Transistor Sizing Of Different Design and Technology
problem: Automatic transistor sizing remains challenging, and existing Bayesian optimization approaches are circuit-specific, preventing accumulation and transfer of design knowledge across different circuits and technology nodes.
motivation: Enabling knowledge transfer across circuits and technology nodes would significantly improve design automation efficiency and reduce simulation costs.
method: KATO uses Bayesian optimization (intelligently learning from each design attempt to guide the next one) to find good transistor sizes. It automatically builds the mathematical models (kernels) needed for this learning. The system reuses knowledge from previous transistor designs for other circuits and older technology nodes, adapting that knowledge to new problems, but filters out knowledge that wouldn't help. It uses Multi-objective Acquisition Ensemble (MACE) to handle multiple competing goals (like speed versus power consumption) when deciding which designs to try next.
key_novelty: It's the first to transfer knowledge from previous transistor designs across different circuits and manufacturing technology nodes when using Bayesian optimization for transistor sizing.
contributions: Efficient automatic kernel construction method for Bayesian optimization
First transfer learning scheme across different circuits and technology nodes for BO
Selective transfer learning mechanism to filter and utilize only useful knowledge
KATO system achieving 2x simulation reduction and 1.2x design improvement
primary_theme: Transfer learning for circuit design automation
